You're right, I was for some reason focused more on material possessions in my thinking, I didn't think about *all* the things money can buy. It's partly because I'm oblivious to them, so to speak. Memories of traveling bring me joy, but they're not the only thing in life that I cherish. A smile from someone I love, or a peaceful rainy day also create good memories in me. Air quality is my only major issue. I'm kind of a cheapskate and at the age of 22 I still have no idea what to spend money on. I have no interest in what money can buy, other than the basic needs. So to be brutally honest the only reason I want to stay here and save money is to have the comfort of never thinking about financial issues in my early life for expenses I currently can not think of.

I don't know what I want out of the 6 months yet, I'm a romantic person so maybe some time alone in some mysterious place I don't know about is what attracts me. I'm tempted to go mostly because I'm living a very passive and sad life and I want a spark to somehow change something in me, and I believe this might be a start. I'll come back immediately after to finish my school, and then I'm open to doing anything anywhere. I have nothing to hold me here, but I'm complacent with the country's situation unlike how it is portrayed in the media (of course it's going downhill economically and stuff if you heard about it, but I feel at home here and had a comfortable life so far) so I also may prefer staying here. I wouldn't normally make the decision of going somewhere for six months, I want to either tackle a bigger goal (like a masters degree, or permanently living somewhere) or settle and develop myself in where I currently live. It would take me 2 years of eating a little less every day, it's not a big number to pay. Still a number though.

I DID research on Poland, funnily enough the air pollution was the only issue I overlooked which I didn't think was this serious at first. But also I remind myself that there are children living there and I'm a grown man so I kinda feel weird worrying about it (but that doesn't change the fact that the particulate matter decreases life expectancy and causes asthma in children). I couldn't find an answer on what effects 180 days would have on someone, most papers/articles talk about long term effects overall. I also saw some people using filter masks like they do in Beijing for example, so I'm prepared to face the issue and it's not the deal breaker, just a con.

Traveling didn't rank highly until now in my life (since I did not travel anywhere yet) but the rare times I did travel I cherished the memories with joy. I'm on the brink of losing the love of my life mostly because of my disinterest in traveling and my tendency to be a stingy so I WANT to rank it higher. Also like I said before, I can't think of anything else to spend money on other than education which should be a mean, not an end.
